appNew.title: New…
appNew.help: Opens the window that makes a project or a document, from any screen

projectNew.title: New project
projectNew.help: Creates an empty project and opens it. A project is the folder holding everything you make: the images, the videos, the sounds, and how they are arranged.

projectOpen.title: Open project
projectOpen.help: Picks a project already on your disk and opens it in place of the current one. The open project is saved as you go, so there is nothing to save first.

documentSaveAs.title: Save as
documentSaveAs.help: Writes a copy of the asset beside the original and carries on with it. The asset that was open stays as it was at the last save.

documentSave.title: Save document
documentSave.help: Writes the document in front into the project. Until it is saved, it lives in the window: the tab carries an asterisk for as long as what is on screen is not what is on disk.

documentClose.title: Close tab
documentClose.help: Closes the document in front. If it holds unsaved work, the studio asks what to do with it. With no tab left, the window closes.

layoutReset.title: Reset layout
layoutReset.help: Puts the panels back where they started. Useful once the windows have been dragged all over and nothing is where you expect. Your work is untouched.

appSettings.title: Settings
appSettings.help: Opens the settings window — this one: the language, the colours, the account, the shortcuts, and everything else that is adjustable.

appAssistant.title: Assistant
appAssistant.help: Opens the window where you say what you want done, by voice or by keyboard. The assistant carries it out itself, and asks for a yes before anything that costs.

appDictate.title: Dictate
appDictate.help: Listens to the microphone and writes what you say at the caret, in the field you are in. Held down by default: speak, let go, the text appears.

windowFullScreen.title: Full screen
windowFullScreen.help: Gives the window the whole screen, with no bar and no border, to work with nothing around it.

spacesMoveLeft.title: Move the space left
spacesMoveLeft.help: Shifts the focused space one place to the left in the top bar. The order you settle on is kept from one session to the next.

spacesMoveRight.title: Move the space right
spacesMoveRight.help: Shifts the focused space one place to the right in the top bar. The order you settle on is kept from one session to the next.

explorerNewFolder.title: New folder
explorerNewFolder.help: Creates an empty folder inside the one the explorer is showing, and opens its name for typing. The folder is yours, as is everything you put in it.

explorerDuplicate.title: Duplicate
explorerDuplicate.help: Lays a copy of each chosen item beside the original, under the first free name. A folder is copied with everything inside it.

explorerCut.title: Cut
explorerCut.help: Holds the selection, to be moved on the next paste. Nothing moves until you paste, and the rows being held are drawn dimmed.

explorerCopy.title: Copy
explorerCopy.help: Holds the selection, to be copied on the next paste. The original stays where it is.

explorerPaste.title: Paste
explorerPaste.help: Drops what the clipboard holds into the folder on screen. An item whose name is already taken is refused, and the rest go through.

explorerTrash.title: Move to trash
explorerTrash.help: Sends the selection to the system trash, where you can get it back. It is the one explorer gesture the studio cannot undo.

explorerUndo.title: Undo the last file gesture
explorerUndo.help: Puts the last batch moved, renamed, duplicated or created back where it was. The stack belongs to the project rather than to a window, and the trash gesture never enters it.

explorerRedo.title: Redo the file gesture
explorerRedo.help: Redoes the batch of files that was just undone, exactly as it was.

sceneSelect.title: Select
sceneSelect.help: The plain tool: click an object in the scene to choose it, without doing anything to it. It is the one you come back to between manipulations.

sceneTranslate.title: Move
sceneTranslate.help: Drags the chosen object from one place to another, by pulling the coloured arrows — one per direction.

sceneRotate.title: Rotate
sceneRotate.help: Turns the chosen object on itself, by pulling the coloured rings — one per axis.

sceneScale.title: Scale
sceneScale.help: Makes the chosen object bigger or smaller, by pulling its handles. Holding Shift keeps its proportions.

sceneFrame.title: Frame selection
sceneFrame.help: Brings the camera close enough that the chosen object fills the view. Handy when you are lost, or when an object is tiny.

sceneFrameFollow.title: Follow the selection
sceneFrameFollow.help: Frames the selection and keeps it in view: whatever moves takes the camera along, at the angle and distance already chosen. Called again, it lets go.

sceneIsolate.title: Isolate selection
sceneIsolate.help: Leaves only the chosen objects on screen while you work on them. Nothing is changed: pressing it again gives the scene back exactly as it was, including the objects you had hidden yourself.

sceneHide.title: Hide selection
sceneHide.help: Takes the chosen objects out of the view without touching the document. Show all brings them back.

sceneShowAll.title: Show all
sceneShowAll.help: Undoes the hiding and isolating done from the viewport. Objects the document itself declares hidden stay hidden.

sceneSnap.title: All snaps
sceneSnap.help: Turns all four snaps on or off at once — surface, grid, angle, scale. A second press gives back exactly the ones that were on. The bar at the top of the viewport sets them one by one.

sceneSpace.title: Local frame
sceneSpace.help: Lines the handles up with the object’s own orientation rather than the world’s. On a turned object, that is what lets you move it “towards its front” rather than north.

sceneProjection.title: Projection
sceneProjection.help: Switches between perspective, where receding lines converge, and orthographic projection, where parallels stay parallel. That is what lets an alignment be judged by eye.

sceneViewFront.title: Look from the front
sceneViewFront.help: Puts the camera in front of the scene, square to the axis. The reference view for judging a silhouette.

sceneViewBack.title: Look from behind
sceneViewBack.help: Puts the camera behind the scene, on the same axis: what the front hides.

sceneViewRight.title: Look from the right
sceneViewRight.help: Puts the camera on the right-hand side, square to the axis. What a depth is judged from.

sceneViewLeft.title: Look from the left
sceneViewLeft.help: Puts the camera on the left-hand side, on the same axis as the right view.

sceneViewTop.title: Look from above
sceneViewTop.help: Puts the camera above the scene, looking straight down. What the objects are laid out on the ground from.

sceneViewBottom.title: Look from below
sceneViewBottom.help: Puts the camera under the scene, looking straight up, the other way from the top view.

sceneViewCamera.title: Look through the camera
sceneViewCamera.help: Draws the view through the chosen camera, and steps back out on a second call. With no camera chosen, it takes the first in the scene.

sceneQuad.title: Four views
sceneQuad.help: Splits the viewport in four — top, front and side around the view being flown. Each quarter orbits under the pointer; the flown one keeps the gizmos.

sceneQuadEdges.title: Quad edges
sceneQuadEdges.help: Redraws the wireframe without the diagonals triangulation added. A GLB never holds quads: this is a reconstruction by angle, faithful except on strongly curved surfaces.

sceneDisplay.title: Display mode
sceneDisplay.help: Cycles what the viewport draws: the surfaces, their edges alone, or both together. The button’s menu picks one directly.

sceneCapture.title: Capture the view
sceneCapture.help: Saves an image of the 3D view into the project’s images — without the grid, the handles or the rails. The menu offers resolutions larger than the panel’s own.

sceneAdd.title: Add
sceneAdd.help: Opens the list of what a scene can take: meshes, lights and objects. A right-click on empty space opens the same list.

sceneAddToSheet.title: Add to the animation band
sceneAddToSheet.help: Puts the selected objects on the band, where keys are set. The band shows only what is put there, so a scene of thousands of objects stays readable.

sceneRemoveFromSheet.title: Remove from the animation band
sceneRemoveFromSheet.help: Removes the line from the band. Keys already set stay, and an object keeps its line for as long as it holds one.

sceneGroup.title: Group
sceneGroup.help: Files the selected objects under one group. Moving the group moves them all, and ⌘Z takes the grouping back.

sceneDuplicate.title: Duplicate
sceneDuplicate.help: Puts a copy of the selection under the same parent and at the very same place, then selects it. A group duplicates whole, with everything hanging from it.

sceneOptimizeSelection.title: Optimise selection…
sceneOptimizeSelection.help: Measures the selection and previews a SAFE runtime representation before changing its optimisation settings.

sceneWorldPerformance.title: World performance…
sceneWorldPerformance.help: Measures the whole scene and reports SAFE optimisation opportunities without changing the authoring world.

sceneExportGame.title: Export the game…
sceneExportGame.help: Builds a standalone game from an optimised runtime copy while leaving the authoring scenes untouched.

sceneCopy.title: Copy
sceneCopy.help: Holds on to the selection so it can be pasted, here or in another scene. This is the studio’s own clipboard: it leaves the system one alone.

sceneCut.title: Cut
sceneCut.help: Holds on to the selection and takes it out of the scene. ⌘Z brings it back.

scenePaste.title: Paste
scenePaste.help: Puts what was copied into the scene in front, and selects it. Pasting twice makes two separate copies.

sceneDelete.title: Delete
sceneDelete.help: Removes everything selected from the scene. Nothing is lost for good: ⌘Z brings it back.

undo.title: Undo
undo.help: Takes back the last thing you did in this document. Each document has its own stack: undo acts on the tab in front, not on the others.

redo.title: Redo
redo.help: Does again what you have just undone. Handy after undoing once too often.

sequencePlayPause.title: Play / Pause
sequencePlayPause.help: Starts playing the edit, or stops it where it is. Starting again picks up where you left off.

sequenceExport.title: Export video…
sequenceExport.help: Writes the edit out as a video file, frame by frame, 3D scenes included. The sound is not in it yet.

sequenceExportCut.title: Export edit (OTIO)…
sequenceExportCut.help: Writes the edit itself out as an OpenTimelineIO file, which other editing applications open — tracks, clips, in points, speeds and links to the media. Fades, gains and image/sound links travel in it too, but only IA Studio reads them back.

sequenceExportEdl.title: Export edit list (EDL)…
sequenceExportEdl.help: Writes the cuts and their timecodes as CMX3600, which every online room reads. The format holds one image track and two sound ones, and nothing of the fades, the gains or the speeds.

sequenceExportFcpxml.title: Export edit (FCPXML)…
sequenceExportFcpxml.help: Writes the edit in the format Final Cut reads and Premiere and Resolve import. The tracks survive, a lane each, and so does the frame size; the fades, the gains and the speeds stay here.

sequenceExportStems.title: Export sound per track (WAV)…
sequenceExportStems.help: Writes one WAV per audible track, mixed the way the edit plays it — the placements, the trims, the fades, the gains and the speeds are baked into the samples. A muted track is not written.

sequenceExportBundle.title: Export edit with its media (OTIOZ)…
sequenceExportBundle.help: Writes the same edit with the media it uses inside the file. This is the one to hand to somebody else, or to open in DaVinci Resolve, which then finds the rushes on its own instead of asking for them one by one.

montageImport.title: Import an edit with its media (OTIOZ)…
montageImport.help: Opens an edit written by another application, rushes and all. The media are copied into the project and enter the catalogue, then the edit opens linked to them. What the opened file does not bring is said as it opens, and starts from its default only there.

sequenceMirror.title: Return window
sequenceMirror.help: Opens the edit in a window of its own, to put on a second screen. It follows the studio frame by frame, without the sound, and closes like any window.

sequenceSplit.title: Split clip
sequenceSplit.help: Cuts the clip in two where the playhead sits, so each half can be handled on its own.

sequenceDelete.title: Delete clip
sequenceDelete.help: Removes the chosen clip from the edit. The original file stays in your assets.

sequenceUnlink.title: Unlink picture and sound
sequenceUnlink.help: Separates the two clips of one take. While they are linked, moving, cutting or deleting one does the same to the other.

sequenceZoomIn.title: Zoom in
sequenceZoomIn.help: Spreads the edit out to see detail: clips get wider and are easier to aim at.

sequenceZoomOut.title: Zoom out
sequenceZoomOut.help: Draws the edit together to see more of it at once, at the cost of the detail.

sequenceFit.title: Fit to view
sequenceFit.help: Sets the zoom so the whole edit fits on screen, end to end.

sequenceStart.title: Go to start
sequenceStart.help: Brings the playhead right back to the beginning of the edit, moving nothing else.

sequenceEnd.title: Go to end
sequenceEnd.help: Sends the playhead right to the end of the edit, past the last clip.

canvasZoomIn.title: Zoom in
canvasZoomIn.help: Magnifies the view one step, around the middle of what is visible. The image itself is untouched — only the way it is looked at.

canvasZoomOut.title: Zoom out
canvasZoomOut.help: Shrinks the view one step, to take in the whole image again.

canvasZoomFit.title: Fit to window
canvasZoomFit.help: Frames the whole image in the panel, with a margin, and never magnifies it past its actual size.

canvasZoomActual.title: Actual size
canvasZoomActual.help: One image pixel per screen pixel: the only scale at which sharpness can be judged.

canvasRulers.title: Rulers
canvasRulers.help: Shows or hides the two graduated rulers, at the top and on the left. Guides are pulled off them.

canvasGuides.title: Guides
canvasGuides.help: Shows or hides the guides laid on the image. Hiding them does not remove them.

canvasGrid.title: Pixel grid
canvasGrid.help: Shows or hides the grid of the artwork’s own pixels. Only on a document set to pixel art.

canvasClearGuides.title: Clear guides
canvasClearGuides.help: Removes every guide from the image. Undoable, like any other edit.

canvasSnap.title: Snap
canvasSnap.help: Makes what is dragged stick to guides, to the image edges and to its centre, within a few pixels.

canvasSelectAll.title: Select all
canvasSelectAll.help: Selects the whole document, which the system’s own select-all cannot do on an image.

canvasDeselect.title: Deselect
canvasDeselect.help: Drops the selected region, so the brush reaches the whole layer again.

canvasCropApply.title: Apply the crop
canvasCropApply.help: Trims the document to the placed frame. ⌘Z gives the frame back, not the pixels.

canvasCropCancel.title: Abandon the crop
canvasCropCancel.help: Takes the crop frame away without trimming anything at all.

canvasMaskFromSelection.title: Make a mask of the selection
canvasMaskFromSelection.help: Hides the active layer outside the selected region.

canvasRegenerate.title: Regenerate the region
canvasRegenerate.help: Asks the model to repaint the masked region of the active layer.

canvasCutout.title: Cut out
canvasCutout.help: Removes the background of the flattened image with the default model.

canvasEnlarge.title: Upscale
canvasEnlarge.help: Raises the resolution of the flattened image with the default model.

canvasVectorize.title: Vectorise
canvasVectorize.help: Turns the flattened image into paths with the default model.

canvasExtend.title: Extend
canvasExtend.help: Asks the model to paint beyond the edges of the flattened image.

canvasMergeDown.title: Merge down
canvasMergeDown.help: Joins the active layer and the one just below it into one, keeping the lower one’s name.

canvasFlatten.title: Flatten image
canvasFlatten.help: Reduces the whole stack to a single layer: hidden layers are dropped, not merged.

canvasFlipHorizontal.title: Flip horizontal
canvasFlipHorizontal.help: Mirrors the whole document left to right, layers included.

canvasFlipVertical.title: Flip vertical
canvasFlipVertical.help: Mirrors the whole document top to bottom, layers included.

canvasRotateCw.title: Rotate clockwise
canvasRotateCw.help: Turns the document a quarter turn to the right: the frame turns with it.

canvasRotateCcw.title: Rotate counter-clockwise
canvasRotateCcw.help: Turns the document a quarter turn to the left: the frame turns with it.

canvasExport.title: Export the image
canvasExport.help: Writes the flattened document to disk, as a PNG.

canvasExportLayered.title: Export the layers (PSD)…
canvasExportLayered.help: Writes the document with its layers, as a Photoshop file. Groups are flattened away: their layers arrive side by side.

skyboxView.title: Change the view
skyboxView.help: Cycles through the four ways of looking at the sky: immersive, panoramic, cross, faces.

skyboxProbes.title: Light probes
skyboxProbes.help: Shows or hides the witness spheres. A sky is judged by what it lights, not by its own image.

canvasToolMove.title: Move tool
canvasToolMove.help: Arms the pointer: a drag moves the active layer, and its handles resize or turn it.

canvasToolHand.title: Hand tool
canvasToolHand.help: Arms the hand: a drag pans the view without touching the document. Holding space does the same without changing tool.

canvasToolCrop.title: Crop tool
canvasToolCrop.help: Arms the crop frame. Draw a frame, then ⏎ to crop or ⎋ to drop it.

canvasToolSelectRectangle.title: Rectangular selection
canvasToolSelectRectangle.help: Arms the rectangular selection. What is selected bounds the brush, the eraser and the bucket.

canvasToolSelectEllipse.title: Elliptical selection
canvasToolSelectEllipse.help: Arms the elliptical selection: a drag inscribes the ellipse in the rectangle swept, and Shift makes it a circle.

canvasToolSelectLasso.title: Lasso
canvasToolSelectLasso.help: Arms the lasso: the selection follows the hand, freehand.

canvasToolShapeRectangle.title: Rectangle shape
canvasToolShapeRectangle.help: Arms drawing a rectangle on the active layer; Shift makes it a square.

canvasToolShapeLine.title: Line shape
canvasToolShapeLine.help: Arms drawing a line. Same group as the rectangle, hence its key with Shift added.

canvasToolShapeArrow.title: Arrow shape
canvasToolShapeArrow.help: Arms drawing an arrow, from where the drag began to where the hand lets go.

canvasToolShapeEllipse.title: Ellipse shape
canvasToolShapeEllipse.help: Arms drawing an ellipse on the active layer; Shift makes it a circle.

canvasToolShapePolygon.title: Polygon shape
canvasToolShapePolygon.help: Arms drawing a regular polygon, whose number of sides is set in the inspector before drawing.

canvasToolShapeStar.title: Star shape
canvasToolShapeStar.help: Arms drawing a star, whose number of points is set in the inspector before drawing.

canvasToolBrush.title: Brush tool
canvasToolBrush.help: Arms the brush, with a softened edge. It paints on the active layer, bounded by the selection when there is one.

canvasToolPencil.title: Pencil tool
canvasToolPencil.help: Arms the pencil, with a hard edge: the same gesture as the brush, without the softening.

canvasToolText.title: Text tool
canvasToolText.help: Arms text: a click places a caption, whose words are typed in the inspector.

canvasToolEraser.title: Eraser tool
canvasToolEraser.help: Arms the point eraser: it clears where the hand passes, bounded by the selection when there is one.

canvasToolFill.title: Paint bucket tool
canvasToolFill.help: Arms the bucket: a click fills the layer, or the selection when there is one.

canvasToolPicker.title: Eyedropper tool
canvasToolPicker.help: Arms the eyedropper: a click takes the colour under the pointer and hands it to the brush.

canvasBrushSmaller.title: Smaller brush
canvasBrushSmaller.help: Narrows the brush, the eraser and the shape stroke by one step of the scale.

canvasBrushLarger.title: Larger brush
canvasBrushLarger.help: Widens the brush, the eraser and the shape stroke by one step of the scale.

sceneSkeletons.title: Show skeletons
sceneSkeletons.help: Draws the bones of every rigged model over the scene.

scenePoseMode.title: Pose mode
scenePoseMode.help: Switches between picking objects and picking the bones of a rig.

sceneNavigate.title: Navigate
sceneNavigate.help: Move through the scene as in a game: the mouse holds the view, W A S D travel, E and Q rise and fall. The wheel sets the speed. Escape gives the mouse back.

sceneNegate.title: Negate
sceneNegate.help: Marks the selected shapes as tools: they are cut out of the others, whichever button is pressed next and in whatever order they were clicked. A marked shape shows translucent red. Press again to take the mark off.

sceneCarve.title: Carve
sceneCarve.help: Cuts the shapes marked Negate — failing that, the smaller ones — out of the biggest selected shape: a cube set inside a wall opens a window in it. The order of the clicks changes nothing. The original shapes are kept — Separate gives them back.

sceneWeld.title: Join
sceneWeld.help: Merges the selected shapes into a single solid. A shape marked Negate is cut out of it instead of being added to it. The original shapes are kept — Separate gives them back.

sceneIntersect.title: Keep overlap
sceneIntersect.help: Keeps only the part where the selected shapes overlap, and throws the rest away. A shape marked Negate is cut out of it instead of being kept. The original shapes are kept — Separate gives them back.

sceneInvertCarve.title: Flip the fold
sceneInvertCarve.help: Folds the same shapes the other way round: what was carved becomes the matter, and the matter becomes the tool. One click, no undo — for the fold that ran backwards.

sceneSeparate.title: Separate
sceneSeparate.help: Breaks a solid apart and gives back the shapes it was made of, each where it stood.
